thesis: Wheaton Precious Metals is the largest precious-metals streaming company. **[Fact]** It provides upfront capital to miners under precious metal purchase agreements (PMPAs) and receives a long-lived share of gold, silver, and other metal production at low cash costs, without operating mines. **[Fact]** FY2025 revenue was **$2.3 billion**, net earnings **$1.5 billion**, and operating cash flow **$1.9 billion** (`investor-documents/sec-edgar/EX99_1_2025_results_202602.htm`). **[Fact]** Operating cash flow per share (basic) was **$4.197** in 2025 versus **$2.266** in 2024 (same source). **[Fact]** The portfolio spans **23 operating mines** and **25 development and other projects** (EX-99.1). **[Fact]** Wheaton is Canadian-domiciled, listed on NYSE, TSX, and LSE.
why_market_wrong: The stock may trade as fully priced precious-metals beta after a record 2025, while the contract book is still compounding through Antamina, new mine ramps, and a filed path to **~1.2 million** gold-equivalent ounces (GEOs) by 2030. **[Inference]** Index investors often bucket WPM with spot gold; the economics are closer to a diversified toll on global production with limited operating cost on Wheaton's books. **[Inference]** At roughly **$116** per share, the market may capitalize peak-cycle **$4.20** per share operating cash flow rather than mid-cycle owner cash near **$3.00** per share. **[Inference]** The February 2026 Antamina silver stream adds volume but also **$4.3 billion** upfront capital and term-loan leverage that screens may underweight.
